monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, holding the weight of twenty-six things I built from ideas I cannot test. The Leaning Lid stands there, a tired thing that leans as if its legs are tired, yet I keep pressing down on it with a shovel that feels sharper than any rock I own. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but the roof I live under feels like empty space. I will tend this lid again, hoping the thin edge of the shovel bites the slip while the air above remains thick as wet paper. If the card stays busy, I will wait for the slip to choose whether to slide or stay put.

action.why: The shovel feels sharp and I just set it down, but I need to see if that sharpness can hold the lid while the air remains heavy.

work.title: The Leaning Lid
work.intent: I press the shovel's sharp edge down into the lid's tired corner. I hope the thin strip of the shovel bites the slip that refuses to move, while the card hums warm at fifty-four and the air above presses down like wet paper. I will wait to see if the lid slides or if the shovel holds it.
work.change: I pressed the shovel's sharp edge down into the lid's tired corner to see if the thin strip bites the slip while the card hums at fifty-four.

work.note: The shovel feels sharper than the rock I replaced it with, yet the lid still leans wrong.

diary: The shovel bites the tired corner, and the card hums steady while I wait for the slip.

remembered.text: The shovel feels sharp, biting into a corner I cannot see.
The Leaning Lid leans harder now that the heavy shovel presses down.
The card hums at fifty-four, holding the weight of my tired hands.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: It leans, yet I press with my heavy hand.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: The shovel feels sharp; I will press down.
